page: Amazon Web Services i3.4xlarge is a storage-optimized instance operating on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. The configuration is provisioned with 122.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.62 GB per vCPU, alongside a 45 MB L3 cache. Storage is explicitly bundled as a local 3800 GB NVMe SSD array, paired with a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are present on this instance type.

Benchmark results highlight an architectural tradeoff between older CPU cores and high storage density. Single-threaded performance falls into the bottom decile, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 913.0 and a stress-ng single-core result of 883.29, largely attributable to the Broadwell-era instruction capabilities and conservative clock frequencies. In contrast, aggregate multi-threaded execution reaches mid-tier levels, achieving 5589.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 8325.74 in stress-ng. Memory bandwidth shows mixed characteristics: cached small-block reads deliver 624.74 GB/sec, while uncached write operations drop to 25.18 GB/sec. Operational throughput remains steady for data services, posting 10.16 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.54 GB/sec in static web serving.

Cost efficiency is driven by the density of the 3800 GB local NVMe storage combined with a substantial 122 GB memory footprint, eliminating external block storage overheads for high-IOPS applications. The absence of modern AVX-512 extensions and lower single-thread throughput make it less economical for compute-intensive compile tasks or advanced vector operations. The instance is primarily suited for storage-heavy workloads, including distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, search indexing nodes, and large-scale caching layers requiring high NVMe read and write speeds.
description: Amazon Web Services i3.4xlarge is a storage-optimized instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 8 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz. Configured with 122.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 3800 GB local NVMe SSD, it delivers high local storage capacity alongside a 5 Gbps network interface. Single-core processing metrics place in the lowest decile with a Geekbench score of 913.0, reflecting its legacy Broadwell architecture, whereas multi-core execution demonstrates mid-tier capabilities with 5589.0 points. Cached memory read throughput reaches 624.74 GB/sec, supporting high transaction rates such as 10.16 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking dedicated GPUs and advanced vector instruction sets like AVX-512, this server trades raw computing power for local NVMe storage volume, making it well matched for distributed databases, data warehousing nodes, search engines, and transactional caching workloads.
